• The house verdict is clear: the eventbus is
  currently a security camera outside the door, not
  the door. Every real mutation happens elsewhere;
  the bus sometimes receives a receipt afterward.

  Only piece.place, map.paint, globals.set, and
  editor.edit exist today in cart/editor/data/
  editorEvents.ts:93, despite the bus contract saying
  callers never mutate directly in runtime/editorbus/
  bus.ts:8.

  Legend:

  - ACTION → REPORT — authored document change;
    consumes that document’s Ctrl‑Z history.

  - PROJECT ACTION → REPORT — map/package/catalog
    mutation; needs an inverse or tombstone, but not
    necessarily canvas Ctrl‑Z.

  - REPORT ONLY — choice, selection, tool, view, or
    session state; never consumes Ctrl‑Z.

  - CONTROL → REPORT — undo, redo, cancel, restore.
  - RECEIPT — currently reaches the bus only after
    mutation.

  - OUTSIDE — currently never reaches the bus.

  ## World and Build

  - Pick/arm a build piece — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Choose Select, Place, Move, Focus, or Paint Faces
    — REPORT ONLY; today inconsistently OUTSIDE from
    the action bar or a generic editor.edit receipt
    from menus/hotkeys.

  - Choose snap mode — REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.
  - Choose active floor — REPORT ONLY; today mostly
    OUTSIDE, with some menu paths producing generic
    receipts.

  - Raise/lower a prop placement ghost — REPORT ONLY;
    today OUTSIDE.

  - Toggle walls down/up — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Select or clear a placed piece — REPORT ONLY;
    today OUTSIDE.

  - Copy a placed piece into the placement hand —
    REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE. The later placement
    is the action.

  - Sample/pick a material — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Place or replace a piece — ACTION → REPORT; today
    typed piece.place RECEIPT after React already
    mutates worldPieces.

  - Move a piece — ACTION → REPORT; today generic
    editor.edit RECEIPT.

  - Rotate a piece — ACTION → REPORT; today OUTSIDE.
  - Delete a piece — ACTION → REPORT; today OUTSIDE.
  - Paint one piece face or all faces — ACTION →
    REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - Assign or clear a material slot — ACTION →
    REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - Set or reset a piece override — ACTION → REPORT;
    today OUTSIDE.

  - Paint, duplicate, or delete a legacy world object
    — ACTION → REPORT; today generic editor.edit
    RECEIPT.

  - Change/reset a physics global — ACTION → REPORT;
    today globals.set is a side-channel receipt
    declared non-undoable, while the state still
    mutates directly.

  ## Maps and Map Paint

  - Create a map — PROJECT ACTION → REPORT; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Rename a map — PROJECT ACTION → REPORT; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Delete a map — PROJECT ACTION → REPORT; today
    OUTSIDE and implemented as immediate directory
    removal.

  - Open/switch/close a map — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Toggle Map Paint — REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.
  - Choose terrain/tile/water/flora/zone/path channel
    — REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.

  - Choose paint/erase, terrain tool, brush shape/
    profile/gizmo, radius, height, slope, or
    smoothing — REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.

  - Pick a tile kind, flora kind, or existing zone —
    REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.

  - Pick a map texture — REPORT ONLY; currently
    MISROUTED. Picking a brand-new texture appends
    the persistent binding table, creates a native
    undo entry, and emits map.paint:tile.bindings.
    Picking an existing texture does not. This
    directly violates the color-choice rule.

  - Add a zone definition — ACTION → REPORT; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Paint/erase a map stroke — ACTION → REPORT; today
    native Map Paint history plus a delayed map.paint
    RECEIPT.

  - Add a path draft point — REPORT ONLY provisional
    state; today OUTSIDE.

  - Undo a draft point — CONTROL → REPORT; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Cancel a path draft — CONTROL → REPORT; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Choose path kind, lanes, sidewalks, tracks,
    level, curve, or stop tool — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Commit a road/light-rail/railway path — ACTION →
    REPORT; today map.paint RECEIPT.

  - Delete a committed path — ACTION → REPORT; today
    map.paint RECEIPT.

  - Place/delete a TC Stop — ACTION → REPORT; today
    map.paint RECEIPT.

  - Add a chunk — ACTION → REPORT; today native
    history plus map.paint RECEIPT.

  - Undo/redo Map Paint — CONTROL → REPORT; today
    restores native snapshots but emits no bus event
    or audit report.

  - Save/autosave painted map — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  ## Mesh Editing

  - Create an unsaved primitive/build/player model
    document — REPORT ONLY until materialized; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Import a model or image into the project —
    PROJECT ACTION → REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - Select a vertex, edge, face, part, or group —
    REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.

  - Choose Move/Scale/Rotate gizmo — REPORT ONLY;
    today OUTSIDE.

  - Toggle mirror-edit X/Y/Z — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Toggle focus, wireframe, camera lock, or lighting
    — REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.

  - Orbit, pan, zoom, frame, or compass-snap the
    camera — REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.

  - Add/remove/move/scale/flip a reference image —
    REPORT ONLY workspace state; today OUTSIDE.

  - Change model decimation quality — ACTION → REPORT
    if it remains saveable model truth; today OUTSIDE
    and outside mesh history.

  - Move/scale/rotate/nudge/scale-by a mesh selection
    — ACTION → REPORT; today native mesh journal,
    OUTSIDE.

  - Extrude edge/face, create face, loop cut, flip
    face, delete selection, or symmetrize — ACTION →
    REPORT; today native mesh journal, OUTSIDE.

  - Detach, merge faces, glass faces, or solidify —
    ACTION → REPORT; today native mesh journal,
    OUTSIDE.

  - Add/import/duplicate/mirror/path-array/delete/
    hide/show/merge parts — ACTION → REPORT; today
    native mesh journal, OUTSIDE.

  - Rename a part or group; group, ungroup, or
    dissolve parts — ACTION → REPORT; today outside
    both the bus and native mesh journal.

  - Edit a model rig — ACTION → REPORT; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Rename/favorite/duplicate/delete a model package
    — PROJECT ACTION → REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - First-save/materialize a model — PROJECT ACTION →
    REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - Save/autosave an existing model revision — REPORT
    ONLY commit result; today OUTSIDE.

  - Export as build piece, prop, player, or NPC —
    PROJECT ACTION → REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - Undo/redo mesh editing — CONTROL → REPORT; today
    native journal only, OUTSIDE.

  ## Model Painting

  - Enter/leave paint mode — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Create the paint atlas/base — ACTION → REPORT;
    today OUTSIDE.

  - Change atlas resolution/budget after creation —
    ACTION → REPORT because it rebuilds document
    paint state; today OUTSIDE.

  - Pick a paint color — REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.
    Its undo behavior is correct.

  - Pick a shader ink — REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.
  - Choose Fill/Brush, preset, size, flow, hardness,
    scatter, detail, or face safety — REPORT ONLY;
    today OUTSIDE.

  - Paint a brush stroke — ACTION → REPORT; today
    native stroke journal, OUTSIDE.

  - Fill a face — ACTION → REPORT; today native
    stroke journal, OUTSIDE.

  - Add a paint layer — ACTION → REPORT; today native
    stroke journal, OUTSIDE.

  - Delete, reorder, or merge paint layers — ACTION →
    REPORT; today native stroke journal, OUTSIDE.

  - Select the active layer — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Show/hide a paint layer — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE and correctly excluded from undo.

  - Rename a paint layer — ACTION → REPORT; today
    serialized metadata outside both bus and stroke
    history.

  - Load a saved paint variant — ACTION → REPORT;
    today directly replaces the active painting,
    OUTSIDE.

  - Save/update/delete a paint variant — PROJECT
    ACTION → REPORT; today direct filesystem writes,
    OUTSIDE.

  - Undo/redo model painting — CONTROL → REPORT;
    today native stroke journal only, OUTSIDE.

  ## Color Studio and Library

  - Choose material, variant, seed, quality, active
    slot, view, or current color — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Pick a tray or scene color — REPORT ONLY; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Fill a material color slot — ACTION → REPORT;
    today generic editor.edit RECEIPT, but Ctrl‑Z
    cannot actually restore it.

  - Reset material slots — ACTION → REPORT; same
    broken generic receipt.

  - Add/load a palette set — ACTION → REPORT in the
    palette/workspace scope; today OUTSIDE.

  - Favorite a material asset — PROJECT ACTION →
    REPORT; today generic receipt, but no matching
    undo restoration.

  - Rename a material asset — PROJECT ACTION →
    REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - Search/filter/select folders, paginate, or focus
    a material document — REPORT ONLY; today OUTSIDE.

  ## Journal, Text, Navigation, and Play

  - Create/rename/describe a build-journal thread —
    PROJECT ACTION → REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - Attach/detach requests or captures — PROJECT
    ACTION → REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - Rate an attempt or crown/uncrown gospel — PROJECT
    ACTION → REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - Edit attribution metadata or export credits —
    PROJECT ACTION → REPORT; today OUTSIDE.

  - Type in a draft text field — REPORT ONLY until
    commit.

  - Commit a rename/text edit — ACTION → REPORT;
    today many fields write durable state on every
    keystroke.

  - Undo/redo focused TextInput text — CONTROL →
    REPORT; today handled by a private 100-entry
    native ring in framework/primitive/input.zig:310,
    entirely outside the bus. Because some fields
    write through per keystroke, this can mutate
    durable truth outside the door.

  - Open/close/select menus, dialogs, panes, tabs,
    documents, diagnostics, or popovers — REPORT
    ONLY; today OUTSIDE.

  - Navigate Editor ↔ Play or router back/forward —
    REPORT/CONTROL; today separate router history,
    OUTSIDE.

  - Choose/rescan an animation camera — REPORT ONLY;
    today OUTSIDE.

  - Live pose samples — sampled system reports; today
    OUTSIDE.

  - Move/look/sprint/jump in /play — future
    replicated gameplay commands plus reports, never
    editor Ctrl‑Z; today entirely outside editorbus.

  - Autosave succeeded/failed, import completed/
    failed, host rejected/clamped, hot reload
    resumed, or compile completed — immutable system
    reports; today status strings, console logs, or
    the diagnostics bus—not the authoring bus.

  ## Logic verification

  The requested sequence works correctly in model
  painting:

  1. Add Layer calls pushUndo("add layer").
  2. Completing the stroke pushes the next undo
     snapshot.

  3. Picking another color changes only the brush
     state.

  4. First Ctrl‑Z removes the stroke.
  5. Second Ctrl‑Z removes the new layer.

  That behavior is established in framework/gpu/
  paint_program.zig:673. The map-texture picker is
  the counterexample because cart/editor/stage/
  mapPaint.ts:267 records a binding-table mutation
  during selection.

  The structural red flags are therefore confirmed:

  - Undoability is not encoded in the durable event
    envelope.

  - Generic editor.edit is always registered as
    undoable even when its source history row says
    otherwise.

  - Undo and redo themselves produce no immutable
    reports.

  - The same command can hit or miss the bus
    depending on whether it came from a menu, hotkey,
    toolbar, viewport, or native loop.

  - No stable action ID ties applied → undone →
    redone reports together.

  - No event records causation/reason or
    distinguishes intent, application, rejection,
    undo, and redo.

  - None of the current event types owns mutation
    authority.

  The loader boundary remains exactly as agreed:
  native pointer projection stays in the split
  framework/world_loader/paint_surface.zig:59 and
  framework/world_loader/paint_runtime.zig:161; the
  semantic stroke must cross the future action door.
  The legacy root loader and geometry remain
  untouched.

  Verification passed:

  zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast test-model-paint
  test-game-map test-world-loader

  No source files were changed during this trace.

• Exactly. Calling both paths select-tool is a naming
  collision, not command unification.

  Today:

  - The action bar directly calls setState in cart/
    editor/shell/AppFrame.tsx:3760.

  - Menus and hotkeys enter cart/editor/shell/
    AppFrame.tsx:620, which can additionally
    manufacture history and a bus receipt.

  Those are two commands that happen to produce the
  same visible state.

  A genuinely single command must look like:

  menu ───────┐
  hotkey ─────┤
  toolbar ────┼─→ one command request ─→ one
  authority door ─→ one handler
  context ────┤                              │
  native input┘                              └─→
  immutable report

  The invocation source is metadata—menu, hotkey,
  toolbar, remote peer—not a reason to select
  different behavior.

  Otherwise:

  - Validation can differ.
  - Undo behavior can differ.
  - Audit coverage can differ.
  - Permissions can be bypassed.
  - Fixes applied to one path leave the other broken.
  - Network replay cannot reproduce local execution
    reliably.

  If two paths genuinely need different semantics,
  they must have different command identities. If
  they claim the same identity, there can be only one
  implementation and one entrance.

  In the house model, these are not two doorknobs on
  the same door. One is a doorknob; the other is a
  separate hole cut through the wall.

  ok so let me just give you the overview without
  drowning you out with too much context here, but
  lets just start at the app runtime itself. What is
  it. It is, zig + react, for a desktop application.
  Now, what is pretty much unanimous about native
  software in the last 30 years. One thing, across
  windows, mac, and even linux, being native isnt
  just a matter of 'you render on the desktop and
  not a browser'; it is quite literally that but its
  much more. File menu controls, settings,
  keybindings, configuration files and not a
  database. etc. And by that short list we can look
  at the first one and just forget about all the
  rest, they actually all happen to tag along with
  it.

  so file menus, why are they special, or atleast
  why are they my focal point. Because in a native
  application, when a feature / command is made, it
  is effectively inherent knowledge  that new
  command 99% of the time means i need a place to
  where the user can call it from. And if that place
  wasnt inside of a file menu, then native desktop
  apps would have css flex already but they dont. So
  that must mean, the file menu is doing a lot more
  lifting than just a 30 some year programming
  default, as it often may seem.

  Now with that in mind step back and look at react
  apps. React, >99% of these apps are web apps, web
  apps, by common stance, efffectively never ship a
  file menu. Now that is not to say that because no
  file menu, functions then live in a crapshoot,
  because they do and they dont. Thing about react
  is that it doesnt care, at all, because its
  conforming to whatever system its built into.
  Thats why when it comes down to things like, key
  bindings, the approach is radically different in
  react-dom to what we have here in reactjit

  And, even as time has passed with how long react
  has been around, React's ecosystem never grew it
  either — and an app built from React's vocabulary
  gets web amnesia by default: keybinds exist in a
  keymap.ts nobody renders, menus are hand-rolled
  divs, right-click is whatever each surface
  improvised, settings are scattered state. Twenty
  years of native convention (the Alt-key
  underlines, the shortcut column, Tools→Options) is
  a discoverability system, and web idiom simply
  never needed it.

  And the settings half deserves equal billing with
  the keybindings half, because it's the same
  missing organ at a different layer: native apps
  have settings as a system — schema'd, persisted
  per-app in the platform's config dir, versioned,
  with the dialog generated from the schema. Web
  apps have localStorage vibes. A framework-tier
  settings primitive (declare schema → get
  persistence, migration, and a rendered preferences
  pane) is the second twenty-years-of-textbook
  organ, and it's what the editor's scattered
  surface presets and physics-globals panels are
  already groping toward ad hoc.
  The strategic note that makes this more than QoL:
  this is the moment ReactJIT's pitch changes.
  "React without the browser" is a performance story
  — impressive, niche. "React semantics with native-
  app organs the web never had" is a category story:
  the framework where a React developer gets a real
  menu bar, real keybindings, real settings, real
  context menus by declaring data, not by fighting
  divs. Nothing in the Electron/Tauri world actually
  offers that — they all inherit web amnesia through
  the DOM.

• Yes. This is the underlying problem, and it is
  larger—and cleaner—than repairing the editor’s
  eventbus one callback at a time.

  The file menu is special because it forces a
  feature to exist independently of its button.

  Web-shaped development tends to begin with:

  button → callback → local mutation

  A native application model begins with:

  command → menu / shortcut / toolbar / context
  menu / palette / remote peer

  That inversion is the missing organ.

  One refinement: the menu should be the mandatory
  public projection and completeness check, while the
  command declaration is the actual authority. Every
  command must either declare a menu location or
  explicitly declare why it is context-only/hidden.
  Nothing becomes undiscoverable accidentally.

  The repository already contains an embryonic
  version of exactly this in runtime/commands/
  command.ts:1. It already says:

  - Register each command once.
  - Reject duplicate command IDs and keybindings.
  - Derive menus and hotkeys from the same command
    object.

  - Commands emit eventbus events and never mutate
    state.

  It landed in a75b8b76a, but the editor subsequently
  built a second system in cart/editor/data/
  commands.ts:1, a second keymap in cart/editor/data/
  keymap.ts:1, and a giant cart-local dispatcher.

  That is extraordinarily useful evidence: making the
  right architecture available is insufficient. It
  must be the framework’s compulsory application
  boundary.

  The completed organ should be:

  Application declaration
  ├── Commands
  │   ├── identity and argument schema
  │   ├── menu path and presentation
  │   ├── default keybinding
  │   ├── enablement/check state
  │   ├── action/report classification
  │   ├── undo scope
  │   └── capability/permission requirements
  │
  ├── Settings
  │   ├── key, type, default, constraints
  │   ├── user/project/session scope
  │   ├── config-file persistence
  │   ├── schema version and migrations
  │   └── generated Preferences presentation
  │
  └── Projections
      ├── native menu bar
      ├── keybinding resolver
      ├── context menus
      ├── toolbars
      ├── command palette
      ├── preferences window
      └── multiplayer/automation API

  Every projection invokes only:

  invoke(commandId, args, source)

  Then:

  invoke
    → validate arguments, scope, enablement,
    permission
    → enter event authority
    → apply through the command’s one handler
    → append immutable report
    → update every projection

  source: "menu" | "hotkey" | "toolbar" | "native" |
  "remote" is audit metadata. It never selects a
  different implementation.

  Settings are the same architecture at another
  layer. A framework SettingDef should produce:

  - The Preferences control.
  - Platform-config persistence.
  - Validation.
  - Migration.
  - Reset-to-default.
  - Searchability.
  - Any menu/keybinding updates that depend upon it.
  - A report whenever it changes.

  And yes: ordinary application preferences should be
  versioned configuration files in the platform’s
  application-config directory, atomically written—
  not values disappearing into the existing SQLite-
  backed __store shim.

  To make bypass genuinely impossible, authoritative
  application state cannot remain ordinary React
  state handed to components with setters. Components
  receive read-only projections. The mutation
  capability belongs only to the command authority.
  Similarly, public Zig bindings cannot expose an
  alternate mutation door to carts; native input must
  submit a semantic command at the transaction
  boundary.

  Even the existing framework-native context menu
  currently stores label + handler in framework/
  primitive/context_menu.zig:1. Under this model it
  should store command references. Then labels,
  shortcuts, enabled state, invocation, and audit
  behavior cannot drift.

  The decisive test is:

  > Can a headless remote peer invoke this command by
  > stable ID, without mounting the UI, and produce
  > the identical validated result?

  If yes, the multiplayer architecture is true.

  If clicking a particular button or calling a
  component callback is required, it is false.
resolution: Completed a read-only reassessment of the editor audit around the proposed ReactJIT native application organ. Confirmed runtime/commands is a tested registry prototype but is unused by cart/editor and does not enforce authority; editorbus only appends receipts; settings/config/menu/context infrastructure is incomplete. Reclassified findings by canonical command identity, authority ownership, and projection/report coverage. Defined the closure path: first unify world.floor.step across menu/hotkey/Section D/headless as a low-risk canary, then migrate world.piece.place as the first authored transaction with validation, one apply, inverse metadata, and correlated outcome; progressively remove cart-local dispatch/setter/native bypasses. Found the exact floor divergence (hotkey wraps and selects Map family; Section D arrows clamp directly), context-menu command bypasses, permanently unavailable roadmap rows in the runtime UI, and a currently failing test-editor-bus compile gate. No source files changed. Verification: runtime command tests 13/13 reported passing; zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast test-editor-bus fails at framework/events/editor_bus.zig:43 due to an import outside module path.
